hero.headline: Nearly 800 arrested after Champions League riots in Paris
hero.body:
Almost 800 people were arrested following violent clashes with police in Paris after the Champions League final between Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal. The disorder resulted in 219 people injured, with 57 of those being police officers.

PSG retained their Champions League title by defeating Arsenal on penalties in the final held in Budapest. The match was decided in a penalty shootout after the teams remained level following extra time. Arsenal's Gabriel Magalhães missed a crucial penalty, while Eberechi Eze also failed to convert from the spot for the Gunners.

Arsenal had taken the lead through Kai Havertz's goal early in the match. The forward latched onto a loose ball near the six-yard box after Leandro Trossard charged down a clearance. Havertz reacted quickly and struck his shot into the roof of the net, with PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov unable to react in time.

PSG equalised through Ousmane Dembélé from the penalty spot in the 65th minute after Cristhian Mosquera made a clumsy challenge on Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. The equaliser came after Arsenal had dominated the first half, with their defensive structure effectively limiting PSG's opportunities. Arsenal's tactical approach focused on compressing spaces and standing firm in one-on-one situations.

The match intensified following the equaliser, with both teams pushing for a winning goal. Neither side could break the deadlock during the remainder of normal time, leading to extra time where nerves became increasingly frayed. When penalties could not separate the teams, Arsenal's hopes ended with Gabriel's miss, as he blazed his effort over the crossbar.

Luis Enrique, PSG's head coach, acknowledged Arsenal's performance after the match. He noted that the Gunners were getting closer to winning major titles and that they played well throughout the final. He praised their ability to control phases of the game that suited their strengths while PSG attempted to dominate possession and apply pressure.

The victory marked PSG's second Champions League title. For Arsenal, the defeat came after they had won the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years earlier in the season. The club's supporters had gathered for a victory parade to celebrate the league triumph despite the heartbreak of the Champions League loss.

The violent clashes that followed PSG's victory represented one of the largest instances of football-related disorder in recent years. French law enforcement faced significant challenges in managing the situation as celebrations deteriorated into chaos across multiple areas of the capital. Fires were set in various locations during the unrest as police worked to restore order and protect public safety.

cards.headline: Trump Changes Terms on Iran Deal, Officials Say
cards.body:
President Trump has modified a draft ceasefire agreement with Iran, according to multiple reports. The changes come as negotiations continue between Washington and Tehran over ending the conflict that began in February.

Trump initially announced on Saturday that a memorandum of understanding had been "largely negotiated" and was close to finalization. However, he walked back those comments on Sunday, insisting that talks were progressing in an "orderly and constructive" manner and that representatives should not rush into an agreement.

"I have informed my representatives not to rush into a deal in that time is on our side," Trump said. He later stressed that no final deal exists yet, telling critics to "don't listen to the losers, who are critical about something they know nothing about."

According to reports, the proposed agreement would include a 60-day ceasefire extension during which Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route it has effectively blocked since the war began. Under the terms, Iran would clear mines from the strait and allow ships to pass freely. In exchange, the United States would lift its naval blockade on Iranian ports, allowing Iran to freely sell oil. Nuclear negotiations would be deferred to a later phase of talks.

The reported concessions from Washington have alarmed several Republican foreign policy hawks who had backed the initial military action against Iran. Senator Roger Wicker, who chairs the Senate Armed Services Committee, called the rumored 60-day ceasefire a "disaster" on social media, warning that "everything accomplished by Operation Epic Fury would be for naught."

Senator Lindsey Graham, a Trump ally, expressed concern that accepting Iran's control over the Strait of Hormuz would represent a "major shift of the balance of power in the region." He questioned why the war began in the first place if the United States was willing to accept these terms. "It makes one wonder why the war started to begin with if these perceptions are accurate," Graham wrote.

Other Republican senators including Tom Cotton and Ted Cruz also voiced opposition to the emerging agreement. Cruz warned that allowing Iran to continue uranium enrichment while receiving billions in sanctions relief would be "a disastrous mistake."

However, Graham later reversed course, hailing Trump's proposal as "brilliant" and suggesting it could expand diplomatic agreements in the Middle East beyond Israel.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the progress "significant" on Sunday. Former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo, who served under Trump's first administration, criticized the proposed deal as "not remotely America First," comparing it unfavorably to the 2015 nuclear agreement that Trump previously abandoned.

The negotiations represent Trump's effort to end the conflict while managing domestic political considerations and international pressure. The exact timeline for reaching a final agreement remains unclear.

cards.headline: Colombia Votes in Presidential Election That Could Reshape US Relations
cards.teaser: Colombians cast ballots in a presidential election held after months of tension between the current president and the White House.
cards.body:
Colombians are casting ballots in the first round of a presidential election that follows months of tension between leftist President Gustavo Petro and US President Donald Trump. The vote serves as a referendum on Petro's policies and presents voters with starkly different visions for the country's future.

The election takes place a decade after Colombia signed a historic peace agreement with the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), ending years of armed conflict. Candidates offer competing approaches to maintaining and building upon that peace settlement.

cards.headline: Israel Seizes Castle in Lebanon as Ground Offensive Expands
cards.body:
Israeli forces have captured Beaufort Castle, a 900-year-old fortress in southern Lebanon, marking their deepest military incursion into the country in more than 26 years. The seizure represents a significant advance against Hezbollah and signals an expansion of Israeli operations beyond previous boundaries.

The castle sits on a commanding hilltop in the Beaufort Ridge area and overlooks much of southern Lebanon. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz confirmed the capture, noting that Israeli and Golani Brigade flags were flying over the fortress. The Israel Defense Forces said it had launched operations in the region to dismantle Hezbollah infrastructure and expand control of the area.

The military operation crossed the Litani River, advancing Israeli forces into territory they had previously occupied between 1982 and 2000. The IDF seized positions from which Hezbollah had coordinated attacks and launched rockets toward Israel. The castle's strategic location provides significant tactical advantages, offering commanding views over southern Lebanon and parts of the western Bekaa valley.

Israeli forces appear to be positioning themselves to potentially encircle Nabatieh, a major city in southern Lebanon that serves as an economic center and cultural heartland. Israeli troops have moved past the towns of Zawtar al-Sharqiyah and Mayfadoun and are approaching Choukine. The military has ordered residents in affected areas to evacuate.

The expansion of ground operations follows stalled negotiations between the United States and Iran. Observers suggest Israeli officials and military commanders want to inflict maximum damage on Hezbollah before any potential deal between Washington and Tehran could limit military operations.

A ceasefire between Israel and Iran-backed Hezbollah officially began on April 17 but has never been observed. Both sides accuse each other of daily violations and justify their attacks based on alleged breaches by the other party.

Lebanon's Prime Minister Nawaf Salam accused Israel of pursuing a "scorched-earth policy and collective punishment" by destroying towns and villages while forcing inhabitants into exile. He called the escalation dangerous and appealed for a swift and genuine ceasefire, though he said the outcome of ongoing negotiations was not guaranteed.

The Lebanese Health Ministry reports that Israeli attacks have killed more than 3,371 people since March 2. Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the wider Middle East conflict in support of Iran, saying it was retaliating for Iran's supreme leader's death in strikes attributed to the United States and Israel.

Hezbollah continued military operations during the offensive, claiming responsibility for targeting the Meron air base in northern Israel and firing rockets toward Kiryat Shmona and Nahariya. The barrage toward Nahariya marked the first rocket fire toward that coastal city in three weeks.

cards.headline: No progress reported on Iran peace deal as negotiations continue
cards.teaser: Efforts to extend a ceasefire with Iran have not yielded results, according to a report on the ongoing negotiations.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card:

Negotiations between the United States and Iran over a ceasefire extension continue without reported progress. While President Trump has suggested a deal may be near, core issues remain unresolved. Trump has not yet decided whether to extend the ceasefire, and Israel continues military operations in Lebanon despite a ceasefire agreement there.

President Trump separately offered to perform at the Freedom 250 event, which marks America's 250th birthday celebration. The offer came after several major musical acts withdrew from the festival.

cards.headline: States Question Costs of Medicaid Work Requirements
cards.teaser: States are raising concerns about the expense of implementing Medicaid work requirements as they face budget constraints.
cards.body:
Multiple states are expressing concern about the cost of implementing new Medicaid work requirements during a period of budget pressure. Oregon Governor Tina Kotek has challenged the new work reporting requirements, warning they could lead to coverage loss for residents.

Montana is moving quickly to adopt the work rules despite budget difficulties. A survey in West Virginia found that most Medicaid recipients are not aware that work requirements are coming. Some analysts warn the changes could force certain early retirees back into the workforce.

cards.headline: Children Detained in ICE Facility, Report Shows
cards.teaser: A report describes children being held in conditions likened to criminal detention inside an ICE facility.
cards.body:
CBS News reported on conditions inside an Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention center where children are being held. According to the report, minors are being detained in conditions comparable to criminal incarceration.

Immigrant detainees have filed a lawsuit against the federal government, alleging inhumane treatment and abuse at Camp East Montana in El Paso, Texas. The detainees describe the conditions as horrific.

cards.headline: Ukraine Denies Drone Hit Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Plant
cards.teaser: Ukraine rejected Russian claims that its drone struck the Zaporizhzhia nuclear facility.
cards.body:
Ukraine's defense forces denied Russian claims that a Ukrainian drone attacked the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant. Russia alleged the strike damaged a turbine building at the facility, Europe's largest nuclear power station.

The International Atomic Energy Agency confirmed a drone attack struck a turbine building at the plant and issued a warning about the incident.

cards.headline: Nearly 800 Arrested After Champions League Riots in France
cards.teaser: Clashes with police during Champions League events resulted in hundreds of arrests and injuries.
cards.body:
Nearly 800 people were arrested following clashes with police at Champions League matches in France. The violent confrontations resulted in 219 injuries, with 57 of those sustained by police officers.

The riots marked one of France's most significant sports-related disturbances in recent years.

cards.headline: Deaths From US Boat Strikes in South America Pass 200
cards.teaser: Coastal residents in Colombia and Ecuador said the airstrike campaign is affecting ocean livelihoods.
cards.body:
Deaths from US boat strikes in Colombia and Ecuador have exceeded 200, according to residents of coastal communities. Local populations said the airstrike campaign has led many to reconsider making a living from the ocean.

The strikes appear to target vessels in waters off the two South American countries. Residents described the campaign as having consequences beyond the death toll for communities that depend on maritime activities.

cards.headline: Retired Nigerian General Abducted With Wife
cards.teaser: The kidnapping of a former military officer highlights ongoing security problems in parts of Nigeria.
cards.body:
Retired Major General Rabe Abubakar and his wife were abducted in northwestern Nigeria. The kidnapping highlights the security challenges that continue to affect parts of the country.

Kidnappings for ransom have become an ongoing problem in several Nigerian states, impacting both civilians and former military officials. The incident reflects broader security concerns in the region.

cards.headline: Five Freed From Flooded Laos Cave, Two Still Missing
cards.teaser: Survivors are helping rescuers plan efforts to locate the last two men trapped in the cave.
cards.body:
Five men have been rescued from a flooded cave in Laos after becoming trapped while searching for gold. The seven villagers entered the narrow tunnel system on May 20, and rescue operations have continued as floodwaters complicated efforts to reach those still inside.

The freed survivors are now helping rescuers develop strategies to locate the two remaining men. Rescue teams are working to navigate the cave's challenging passages and water-filled sections to bring them to safety.

cards.headline: Judge Blocks Trump's Kennedy Center Changes
cards.teaser: A federal judge ruled that President Trump's name must be removed from the Kennedy Center.
cards.body:
A judge has blocked changes President Trump attempted to make at the Kennedy Center and ordered his name removed from the performing arts venue. The President responded with public criticism of the judge who issued the ruling.

Trump released a lengthy statement about the decision. The ruling affects Trump's attempts to alter the Kennedy Center, a national cultural institution in Washington. The judge's order requires the removal of Trump's name from the building.

cards.headline: Experimental Pill Extends Lives of Pancreatic Cancer Patients
cards.teaser: A new pill helped people with advanced pancreatic cancer live longer in clinical research.
cards.body:
Researchers reported that a novel pill extended the lives of people with advanced pancreatic cancer. The experimental treatment offers potential progress against one of the deadliest forms of cancer.

Pancreatic cancer has historically had limited effective treatment options. The pill represents a new approach that showed benefits for patients with advanced disease. Researchers described the findings as raising hopes for better treatments for this type of cancer.

cards.headline: Israel Day Parade Returns to New York with Heavy Police Presence
cards.teaser: The annual Israel Day Parade will take place in New York City with increased security and notable political absences.
cards.body:
The Israel Day Parade is returning to New York City with organizers expecting record turnout. Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced he will skip the parade but pledged a large police presence for security.

Multiple streets will be closed for the event. Authorities have released details on the parade route and road closures throughout the city. The parade takes place against what has been described as a changed backdrop, though specific details about those changes were not provided in the available information.

cards.headline: Israel Captures Medieval Castle in Lebanon Offensive
cards.teaser: Israeli forces seized the 12th-century Beaufort Castle as part of an expanded military operation in southern Lebanon.
cards.body:
Israel has captured Beaufort Castle, a 12th-century fortress that overlooks southern Lebanon and northern Israel. The seizure is part of a major ground offensive that Israel has expanded in southern Lebanon.

The Israeli military has ordered all residents south of the Zahrani River to evacuate. The capture of the strategic castle suggests Israel is planning an extended military presence in the region.

hero.headline: Lung Cancer Drug Reduced Death Risk by 34% in China Trial
hero.body:
A pharmaceutical treatment called ivonescimab demonstrated a significant survival benefit in patients with squamous cell lung cancer during a late-stage clinical trial conducted in China. The drug, developed by Chinese company Akeso in partnership with Summit Therapeutics, reduced the risk of death by 34% compared to standard treatment approaches.

The trial compared ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy against a control group receiving a PD-1 inhibitor paired with chemotherapy. Patients who received ivonescimab experienced longer survival times than those in the comparison group. The findings are specifically relevant to squamous cell lung cancer, which is a subtype of non-small cell lung cancer.

What distinguishes ivonescimab from existing treatments is its dual mechanism of action. The drug targets two separate pathways in the immune system simultaneously, whereas current PD-1 inhibitors focus on only one pathway. This approach has sparked considerable discussion within the pharmaceutical industry about whether it offers meaningful advantages over treatments already available to patients.

Akeso developed the drug in China, where the company is headquartered. Summit Therapeutics holds the rights to develop and commercialize ivonescimab in markets outside greater China, including the United States and Europe. Both companies are pursuing expanded use of the medication based on these trial results and ongoing research.

The 34% reduction in death risk represents a statistically significant improvement over the control treatment. The trial specifically examined patients receiving chemotherapy combinations, which represents a standard approach for treating many lung cancer patients.

Squamous cell carcinoma represents a substantial portion of non-small cell lung cancer cases worldwide. The introduction of new treatment options could influence clinical decision-making for physicians treating this patient population. Lung cancer continues to rank among the leading causes of cancer deaths globally, making advances in treatment particularly important.

The research team presented these results at a major medical conference where they attracted attention from oncologists and industry professionals. The presentation highlighted the potential for ivonescimab to become an important addition to the available immunotherapy options for lung cancer patients.

Moving forward, regulatory agencies will review the trial data to determine whether ivonescimab qualifies for approval in additional markets. Both Akeso and Summit Therapeutics are preparing submissions to health authorities based on these findings and supporting evidence from other ongoing studies. The approval process will ultimately determine whether the drug becomes available to a broader population of lung cancer patients seeking new treatment alternatives.

cards.headline: China Factory Activity Stalls as Demand Weakens
cards.teaser: Manufacturing activity in China remained flat in May as demand declined and energy costs rose.
cards.body:
China's factory activity showed no growth in May, according to purchasing managers index data released Sunday. The stagnation signals continued weakness in the country's manufacturing sector as demand softens.

Energy costs weighed on production during the month. The flat reading raises questions about the strength of China's economic recovery and suggests manufacturers continue to face headwinds from both domestic and international markets.

cards.headline: Elon Musk Pursuing Merger Between SpaceX and Tesla
cards.teaser: Musk is pushing to combine SpaceX and Tesla into a single company valued at $3.4 trillion, though analysts say the merged entity would initially lose money.
cards.body:
Elon Musk is working toward merging SpaceX and Tesla into one corporation with a potential valuation of $3.4 trillion. The move comes as Musk pushes SpaceX toward a public listing on the Nasdaq stock exchange.

Financial analysts have raised concerns that the combined company would lose money from its first day of operation. Some Tesla shareholders have expressed opposition to the merger plan, though Musk continues to pursue the consolidation of his two largest business ventures.

cards.headline: Electric Air Taxi Demonstrated in New York City
cards.teaser: Aviation startup Joby completed a test flight of its all-electric aircraft in Manhattan, though the vehicles still require regulatory approval before public use.
cards.body:
Joby Aviation flew its electric air taxi in New York City as part of a demonstration of the new aircraft technology. The company and other aviation startups are working with the Trump administration on plans to replace helicopters with electric aircraft for urban transportation.

The vehicles still face extensive testing requirements before they can carry passengers. Regulators must approve the aircraft and operating procedures before the public can use them for commercial flights. The demonstration represents a step toward potential future deployment of electric air taxis in major cities.

cards.headline: United Airlines Flight Returns After Bluetooth Security Alert
cards.teaser: A United Airlines Boeing 767 flying from Newark to Spain turned back mid-ocean after a passenger's Bluetooth device name triggered a security alert.
cards.body:
United Airlines flight UA236 from Newark Liberty to Palma de Mallorca declared an emergency and returned to Newark after crew members detected a Bluetooth device with a name that raised security concerns. The transatlantic flight turned around over the Atlantic Ocean.

Passengers reported that a boy had named his Bluetooth device with a word that resembled a security threat. The incident disrupted service on the transatlantic route. The aircraft landed safely back at Newark after the crew followed security protocols.

cards.headline: Airbnb Expands Beyond Home Rentals to Hotels and Car Rentals
cards.teaser: The home-sharing platform has added car rentals, groceries, and hotels to its app as CEO Brian Chesky redesigns the service.
cards.body:
Airbnb has expanded its offerings beyond home rentals to include car rentals, grocery delivery, and hotel bookings. Brian Chesky, the company's co-founder and chief executive, is leading efforts to redesign the platform and broaden its services.

The addition of hotels represents a shift for a company originally built on connecting travelers with people renting out their homes. Chesky continues to explore ways to transform the app into a broader travel and lifestyle service beyond its original business model.

cards.headline: Beer Industry Looks to World Cup to Reverse Sales Decline
cards.teaser: Brewers are hoping the soccer tournament will boost beer sales after a period of declining demand in the US market.
cards.body:
The maker of Budweiser and Michelob Ultra is investing heavily in World Cup marketing to combat declining US beer sales. The company is banking on the global soccer tournament to generate consumer interest and boost demand for its products.

Bars and retailers remain skeptical about whether the event will drive significant increases in beer purchases. Still, Anheuser-Busch InBev is committing substantial resources to capitalize on the World Cup's reach and appeal.

hero.headline: Microsoft threatens security researchers with criminal investigation over exploit disclosure
hero.body:
Microsoft threatened a cybersecurity researcher with criminal investigation after the researcher disclosed security vulnerabilities in the company's products. Multiple outlets reported the incident, with one researcher stating the company told them "they will ruin my life."

The dispute centers on how security researchers should handle zero-day exploits, which are previously unknown software vulnerabilities. Microsoft's response to the disclosure has drawn criticism from the security community.

One security researcher described feeling humiliated by Microsoft's approach and pledged what they called a "bone shattering drop" in response. The researcher's comments suggest they plan to release additional information about security flaws.

The incident has sparked debate about Microsoft's policies on vulnerability disclosure. Security experts have criticized the company's stance, with one commentator describing it as "a dumpster fire of their own making."

Zero-day exploits represent a significant security concern because they can be used to attack systems before patches are available. The security research community generally operates under disclosure frameworks meant to give companies time to fix vulnerabilities before making them public.

Microsoft's decision to involve law enforcement in this case marks an escalation in how the company handles security researchers. The approach contrasts with bug bounty programs that many technology companies use to reward researchers who find and report vulnerabilities.

The researcher facing threats from Microsoft expressed fear about the potential consequences. Their statement about having their life ruined reflects concerns about both legal action and professional reputation.

The controversy highlights ongoing tension between technology companies and independent security researchers. Companies want to control how information about their products' vulnerabilities becomes public, while researchers argue transparency serves the broader interest of cybersecurity.

Multiple publications covered the story, indicating widespread interest in the security community. The incident has prompted discussions about whether Microsoft's current policies adequately balance security concerns with the need for researcher cooperation.

cards.headline: Enhanced Games featured athletes using performance-enhancing drugs
cards.teaser: A sporting competition where most athletes used performance-enhancing drugs took place in Las Vegas.
cards.body:
The Enhanced Games, held in Las Vegas, featured a competition where a majority of athletes used performance-enhancing drugs. The event represents a departure from traditional sporting competitions that ban such substances.

The competition may signal a new business model that the technology industry is prepared to support. The event combined athletics with an approach that accepts rather than prohibits drug use among competitors.

cards.headline: Rising temperatures impair cognitive function in animals
cards.teaser: Heat affects animal behavior and learning ability as temperatures climb.
cards.body:
Animals experience impaired brain function as temperatures rise, according to new research. Some creatures become more aggressive while others struggle to learn when exposed to high heat.

The cognitive effects of extreme temperatures add another dimension to understanding how climate affects wildlife. The research documents behavioral changes linked specifically to heat exposure in various species.

cards.headline: Nest of endangered curlew discovered in conservation area
cards.teaser: A conservation trust posted video of a curlew nest containing eggs.
cards.body:
The Sliabh Beagh Curlew Conservation Trust posted video footage showing a curlew nest with eggs. The organization described the bird as remarkable.

Curlews are an endangered species, making nest discoveries significant for conservation efforts. The trust documented the finding as part of its work to protect the bird population in the area.

cards.headline: Hindhead Tunnel project leads to successful rewilding in southern England
cards.teaser: A lost road helped create one of the most successful rewilding projects in the region.
cards.body:
The Hindhead Tunnel project transformed a former road corridor into a rewilding success story in southern England. The infrastructure change created conditions that allowed natural habitats to recover.

The project represents one of the most effective rewilding initiatives in the southern part of the country. The conversion of the road area into natural landscape demonstrates how infrastructure projects can sometimes benefit conservation when properly managed.

cards.headline: Little Nightmares 2 Enhanced Edition released for Nintendo Switch 2
cards.teaser: The enhanced version of the game is now available on the new console platform.
cards.body:
Little Nightmares 2 Enhanced Edition is now available on Nintendo Switch 2. The horror puzzle game arrives on Nintendo's latest console following an extended development period.

The enhanced edition has been optimized to leverage the Switch 2's hardware capabilities, delivering an updated experience for players on the new platform.

cards.headline: Thermal Grizzly developing WireView Pro II in partnership with Noctua
cards.teaser: The company is preparing a new version of its GPU power monitoring device for 12V-26 graphics cards.
cards.body:
Thermal Grizzly announced it is developing the WireView Pro II Noctua Edition, designed for 12V-26 GPUs. The device monitors power delivery to graphics cards.

The collaboration with Noctua represents a partnership between two companies known for cooling and monitoring products. The new version appears aimed at compatibility with upcoming graphics card power standards.

He noted that the Gunners were getting closer to winning major titles and that they played well throughout the final. He praised their ability to control phases of the game that suited their strengths while PSG attempted to dominate possession and apply pressure.

The victory marked PSG's second Champions League title. For Arsenal, the defeat came after they had won the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years earlier in the season. The club's supporters had gathered for a victory parade to celebrate the league triumph despite the heartbreak of the Champions League loss.

The violent clashes that followed PSG's victory represented one of the largest instances of football-related disorder in recent years. French law enforcement faced significant challenges in managing the situation as celebrations deteriorated into chaos across multiple areas of the capital. Fires were set in various locations during the unrest as police worked to restore order and protect public safety.

cards.headline: Marta Kostyuk defeats four-time French Open champion Iga Swiatek
cards.teaser: Marta Kostyuk knocked out four-time French Open champion Iga Swiatek in the fourth round at Roland-Garros.
cards.body:
Marta Kostyuk delivered a stunning upset at Roland-Garros, eliminating third seed Iga Swiatek in the fourth round with a dominant 7-5, 6-1 victory. The 15th-seeded Ukrainian's commanding performance ended Swiatek's tournament run and continued her impressive form at this year's French Open.

The loss proved particularly difficult for Swiatek, who suffered the defeat on her 25th birthday. Once a fortress on Court Philippe-Chatrier, the four-time French Open champion struggled through what she later described as her most challenging performance in Paris in recent years, marking a rare early exit for the dominant player.

cards.headline: Liverpool fires manager Arne Slot after less than a season
cards.teaser: Liverpool dismissed manager Arne Slot, with sporting director Richard Hughes reversing his earlier support for the coach.
cards.body:
Liverpool has dismissed manager Arne Slot following a disappointing tenure marked by tactical struggles and a disconnect with supporters. Under Slot's leadership, the team played a cautious style of football that failed to dominate opponents, leaving fans yearning for the attacking flair associated with previous Liverpool sides.

The new manager will face significant challenges at Anfield, including implementing an attractive attacking style and rebuilding the bond between the club and its supporters. Slot's inability to combine compelling football with results proved costly, as he lacked both the commanding personality of predecessor Jürgen Klopp and the on-pitch success needed to win over the fanbase.

cards.headline: Manchester United teenager Tyler Fletcher added to Scotland World Cup squad
cards.teaser: Tyler Fletcher, a Manchester United teenager, was called up to Scotland's World Cup squad as a late replacement for injured Billy Gilmour.
cards.body:
Tyler Fletcher has been called up to Scotland's World Cup squad as a late replacement for injured midfielder Billy Gilmour. The Manchester United teenager's selection comes after minimal playing time at club level.

Fletcher's inclusion marks a dramatic change in circumstances. He had anticipated attending the World Cup as a spectator this summer, but now has the chance to represent Scotland in the tournament itself.

cards.headline: Caitlin Clark benched after confrontation with coach Stephanie White
cards.teaser: Caitlin Clark was benched during the Indiana Fever's loss to the Portland Fire after a heated exchange with coach Stephanie White.
cards.body:
Caitlin Clark was pulled from the game against the Portland Fire following a heated exchange with head coach Stephanie White. Clark finished with just six points in the Fever's loss.

The Portland Fire dominated the Indiana Fever in front of a sold-out crowd that set a new attendance record for the team. Clark's limited performance marked a significant departure from her typical output.

cards.headline: Chicago Bears stadium funding bill collapses before Illinois legislative deadline
cards.teaser: A bill to provide property tax breaks and funding for a new Chicago Bears stadium broke down before the Illinois legislative deadline.
cards.body:
The Chicago Bears' proposed stadium funding bill failed to advance as the Illinois spring legislative session entered its final hours. Lawmakers had been considering a megaprojects bill that included property tax breaks for the team.

Legislators are attempting to craft an alternate plan as the session deadline approaches. The breakdown of the original bill leaves uncertainty about whether state assistance will be provided to help keep the Bears in Illinois.

cards.headline: Elisa Balsamo wins second stage of women's Giro d'Italia
cards.teaser: Race leader Elisa Balsamo strengthened her position at the top of the women's Giro d'Italia by winning the second stage.
cards.body: The victory reinforces Balsamo's standing at the top of the general classification as the multi-stage race continues.

hero.headline: Matt Brown, Alaskan Bush People Star, Dies at 43
hero.body:
Matt Brown, a cast member of the Discovery Channel reality series Alaskan Bush People, has died at age 43. His body was pulled from a river, according to family members.

Brown's brother Noah helped recover his body from the river. His brother Bear also confirmed the death. The exact circumstances surrounding Brown's death have not been detailed publicly.

Brown appeared on Alaskan Bush People, which followed the Brown family living in remote areas of Alaska. The show documented their lifestyle away from modern civilization. Matt Brown was the eldest of the Brown siblings featured on the program.

The Discovery Channel series premiered in 2014 and ran for multiple seasons. The show gained a following for its portrayal of the family's off-grid lifestyle in the Alaskan wilderness.

Matt Brown had previously dealt with personal struggles that were documented on the show and in public statements. He had taken breaks from filming during the series' run.

The Brown family has dealt with multiple losses in recent years. The family patriarch, Billy Brown, died in 2021. The family has continued to share updates about their lives through social media and television appearances.

Discovery Channel has not yet released a statement about Brown's death. Family members began sharing news of his passing through social media and public statements.

Brown's death marks another loss for the reality television community. Alaskan Bush People developed a dedicated audience during its years on air, with viewers following the family's journey and personal challenges.

The series showed the Brown family building homes, hunting for food, and navigating life in remote wilderness areas. Matt Brown was featured prominently in early seasons of the show before stepping back from regular appearances.

cards.headline: A24's Backrooms Opens With Record-Breaking $81 Million Weekend
cards.teaser: The horror film collected $81 million from North American theaters in its opening weekend.
cards.body:
A24's horror film Backrooms shattered the studio's previous opening weekend record, earning $81 million across North America. Directed by Kane Parsons, the film pulled in $38 million on its opening day alone, far exceeding industry expectations. The strong debut toppled A24's prior record of $25.5 million set by Alex Garland's Civil War.

The film attracted massive crowds of younger moviegoers to theaters nationwide. The weekend proved exceptional for horror at the box office, with another horror film, Obsession, also seeing significant attendance gains. Meanwhile, The Mandalorian and Grogu experienced a steep 70 percent drop in ticket sales from its previous weekend.

cards.headline: Trump Offers to Perform at Freedom 250 Concert After Artists Cancel
cards.teaser: The former president proposed performing himself at the planned celebration after multiple musical acts withdrew.
cards.body:
Donald Trump said he would perform at the Freedom 250 concert series after several musical artists withdrew from the event. Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels, and country singer Martina McBride all dropped out, citing concerns that the event would become political.

Following the cancellations, Trump attacked the departing artists and suggested alternatives to the concert series, including potentially holding a rally instead. He stated that only great patriots would be invited to participate in any performances.

cards.headline: Italy Bans Upcoming Kanye West and Travis Scott Concerts
cards.teaser: Italian authorities canceled concerts scheduled for July in Reggio Emilia, citing security concerns.
cards.body:
Italian authorities cancelled a Kanye West concert scheduled for July 18 at the RCF Arena in Reggio Emilia. The city's prefect, Salvatore Angieri, made the decision citing "public order and safety issues" following concerns raised by the local Jewish community about West's previous antisemitic remarks.

West, who changed his name to Ye in 2021, was set to perform at the Pulse of Gaia festival. The cancellation reflected growing scrutiny of the rapper's conduct and statements in recent years.

cards.headline: Only Murders in the Building Wins Outstanding Scripted Series at CrimeCon Clue Awards
cards.teaser: The Hulu comedy took top honors at the awards ceremony recognizing crime-related entertainment.
cards.body:
Only Murders in the Building won the award for outstanding scripted series at the 2026 CrimeCon Clue Awards. Hulu led the ceremony with two major category wins.

The streaming service also won outstanding docuseries for Girl on the Run: The Hunt for Americas Most Wanted. CBS's 48 Hours was among other winners announced at the awards ceremony, which took place Saturday and recognizes crime-focused television programming and podcasts.

cards.headline: Brazil Launches Free Government Streaming Service Tela Brasil
cards.teaser: President Lula da Silva announced the platform offering 555 Brazilian productions at no cost.
cards.body:
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced the creation of Tela Brasil, a free streaming service offering Brazilian productions. The platform launched with an initial catalog of 555 titles.

Anyone with an account on Gov.br, the official digital platform of the Brazilian federal government, can access Tela Brasil. Lula made the announcement at Rio2C, a major entertainment and technology conference held in Rio de Janeiro.

cards.headline: Jay-Z Performs at Philadelphia's Roots Picnic With Jazmine Sullivan, Bilal and Meek Mill
cards.teaser: The rapper headlined the festival and changed his streaming name back to its original spelling.
cards.body:
Jay-Z headlined the Roots Picnic in Philadelphia with guest appearances from Jazmine Sullivan, Bilal and Meek Mill. The performance brought what was described as New York style to the Philadelphia festival.

Jay-Z had recently changed his name on streaming platforms from Jay-Z to its original spelling, JA-Z. The name change preceded his Roots Picnic performance and may have signaled the direction of the show.

hero.headline: Virginia Governor Spanberger faces Democratic backlash over legislative vetoes
hero.teaser: Gov. Abigail Spanberger is drawing criticism from members of her own party after vetoing 31 bills passed by the Democratic-led Virginia legislature.
hero.body:
Abigail Spanberger, Virginia's newly elected governor, has drawn criticism from her own party after vetoing 31 bills passed by the Democratic-controlled state legislature. The conflict highlights disagreements within the party about the state's policy direction going forward.

Spanberger, a former CIA officer and federal law enforcement agent who previously served three terms in the U.S. House of Representatives, won the gubernatorial race decisively. She defeated Republican Lieutenant Governor Winsome Earle-Sears with 57 percent of the vote to Earle-Sears' 43 percent, according to the Associated Press.

In her victory speech, Spanberger emphasized pragmatism and bipartisanship. "We sent a message to every corner of the commonwealth, a message to our neighbors and our fellow Americans across the country," she told supporters in Richmond. "We chose pragmatism over partisanship. We chose our commonwealth over chaos."

Spanberger's election as Virginia's first female governor came as part of a strong night for Democrats across the state. Ghazala Hashmi, a state Democratic senator, won the lieutenant governor's race and became the first Muslim woman elected to statewide office in the United States. Democrat Jay Jones defeated Republican Attorney General Jason Miyares, and state Democrats expanded their majority in the House of Delegates by flipping several Republican-held districts.

The Democratic victories create what is known as a governing trifecta, giving the party control of the governor's office and both chambers of the legislature. This control positions Virginia as a state likely to oppose Trump administration policies and will allow Democrats to redraw congressional maps in their favor.

During her campaign, Spanberger emphasized her record in Congress as the most bipartisan member from Virginia. Rather than focusing on attacking Trump directly, she concentrated on Democratic proposals to guarantee healthcare and lower the cost of living. However, in her victory speech, she addressed concerns about federal employment and the economy.

"To those across the Potomac who are attacking our jobs and our economy, I will not stand by silently while you attack Virginia's workers," Spanberger said. "I will fight every single day for every single Virginia job and I will stand up to anyone who tries to harm our economy or the livelihoods of our Virginians."

Spanberger's approach differed from her Republican opponent's strategy. Earle-Sears, the first woman of color elected to statewide office in Virginia, centered her campaign on cultural issues that had helped boost Trump's candidacy. Her loss continued what has been called "the Virginia curse," where the party out of the White House has won the governor's mansion in nearly every election since 1976.

cards.headline: Newark mayor orders curfew around immigration detention center after days of clashes
cards.teaser: Newark Mayor Ras Baraka ordered a curfew around an immigration detention center where protesters and law enforcement officers have clashed for days.
cards.body:
Newark Mayor Ras Baraka ordered a curfew around an immigration detention center where protesters and law enforcement officers have clashed for days. The mandatory curfew covers a half-mile area surrounding Delaney Hall and took effect immediately.

The curfew begins at 12 a.m. each night. Baraka cited the need to ensure the safety and well-being of all residents in announcing the measure.

Protesters gathered outside Delaney Hall in Newark over the past week in solidarity with detained migrants. Sen. Andy Kim met with demonstrators outside the facility last weekend.

Kim called the week of clashes one of the most difficult of his life. The New Jersey Democrat spoke about the situation after meeting with protesters who had assembled at the federal immigration detention center.

The protests centered on conditions inside Delaney Hall, where migrants are being held in federal custody. Law enforcement officers and demonstrators have faced off repeatedly at the site over multiple days.

Baraka implemented the geographic restriction to try to restore order to the area around the detention facility. The curfew applies to everyone within the designated half-mile zone surrounding Delaney Hall.

The mayor framed the decision as a public safety measure for Newark residents. He did not specify how long the curfew would remain in effect or what penalties would apply for violations.

Kim attended the protests last weekend as tensions escalated between demonstrators and police. The senator described the experience and its aftermath as among the most challenging periods of his career in public service.

The clashes mark an escalation in demonstrations related to immigration detention in the Newark area. Protesters have focused their efforts on drawing attention to conditions faced by migrants held at Delaney Hall.

cards.headline: World Food Program director asks Trump administration for increased food aid
cards.teaser: Cindy McCain, who leads the World Food Program, pressed the Trump administration for more food assistance in an interview with CBS News.
cards.body:
World Food Program Executive Director Cindy McCain called on the Trump administration to provide more food aid. McCain told CBS News that her organization needs help.

CBS News host Margaret Brennan asked McCain whether the dismantling of the U.S. Agency for International Development has affected the places where the World Food Program operates. McCain responded by emphasizing the need for additional support from the administration.

cards.headline: No progress reported on Iran peace deal as negotiations continue
cards.teaser: Efforts to extend a ceasefire with Iran have not yielded results, according to a report on the ongoing negotiations.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card:

Negotiations between the United States and Iran over a ceasefire extension continue without reported progress. While President Trump has suggested a deal may be near, core issues remain unresolved. Trump has not yet decided whether to extend the ceasefire, and Israel continues military operations in Lebanon despite a ceasefire agreement there.

President Trump separately offered to perform at the Freedom 250 event, which marks America's 250th birthday celebration. The offer came after several major musical acts withdrew from the festival.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: Former federal prosecutor Ankush Khardori discussed the unusual nature of the Justice Department's criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll.
cards.body:
A criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll originating from U.S. Attorneys offices around the country is drawing attention for its unusual characteristics. Former federal prosecutor Ankush Khardori spoke with NPR about the case.

Khardori, a former Justice Department official, addressed questions about investigations and prosecutions coming from federal prosecutors' offices. He characterized the Carroll investigation as atypical compared to standard Justice Department procedures.

cards.headline: Social Security retirement age change affects 2026 retirees
cards.teaser: People planning to retire in 2026 may face unexpected impacts on their Social Security benefits due to a retirement age change.
cards.body:
The retirement age changed in 2026, catching some prospective retirees off guard. People who entered the year thinking they were ready to retire may not meet the new age threshold.

Retiring this year without meeting the specific age requirement could significantly impact Social Security benefits. The change applies to people within a particular age range who had planned to begin collecting benefits in 2026.

cards.headline: Worst wheat crop in decades expected to raise grocery prices
cards.teaser: Wheat farmers are experiencing their worst crop in decades due to poor growing conditions, which could soon affect consumer prices.
cards.body:
Wheat farmers are facing their worst crop yields in decades this year. A combination of poor conditions has created major problems for wheat production across the country.

Consumers can expect to see ripple effects at grocery stores soon as a result of the poor harvest. The reduced wheat supply is likely to push up prices for products that rely on wheat as a primary ingredient.
